title: Cross-environment canary rollback orchestration for multi-tenant model regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments observed quality regressions and sporadic token truncation after the 2026-03-09 model rollout (model v3.4-quant). Problem pattern: regressions appear in canary cohort with increased token drop and higher per-token latency for long-context prompts. The regression surfaced differently per environment: Hosted showed transient 5-10s tail latency spikes during peak traffic, Dedicated tenants reported KV-cache desync on pooled GPUs producing truncated completions, and a customer on Private on-prem noted OOMs in a specific quantized kernel path. Objective: coordinate a single orchestration runbook that safely pauses rollouts, executes environment-specific quick-fixes (fallback to previous model variant or kernel path), performs customer-facing verification, and sequences full rollback where necessary. Scope: orchestration for canary cohorts, dedicated tenant pools, and private air-gapped installs; communications to CS/SRE and impacted customers; automated rollback triggers in the control plane; postmortem and mitigations for kernel selection and cache invalidation. Proposed actions: 1) Pause all ongoing rollouts and mark v3.4-quant as quarantined in model catalog. 2) For Hosted: trigger automatic fallback to v3.3-stable for traffic routed from canary routes; increase read-through cache TTL and enable prefix caching to reduce token regen. 3) For Dedicated: isolate affected GPU pool, flush KV caches and restart worker processes with v3.3-stable runtime image. 4) For Private: produce a signed hotfix package and coordinate an expedited on-prem upgrade with the customer's infra lead; provide rollback script and manual verification checklist. 5) Update control-plane orchestrator to add a canary rollback policy that considers latency delta and token loss rate as triggers. Risks & trade-offs: rolling back reduces exposure but may hide a deeper incompatibility between quantized kernels and newer runtime optimizations; immediate kernel disable may increase latency/cost. Communication: provide templated emails and Slack playbooks for CS/SRE to notify impacted customers with remediation steps and ETA. Links to artifacts and runbooks are in attachments. Acceptance criteria specified below.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial detection from Hosted telemetry (route: canary-eu). Spike in token-drop rate at 02:18 UTC. Notified on-call and created this issue to consolidate cross-env actions.

2026-03-10 - Marco Li: Triage complete. Hypothesis: quantized kernel selector (auto-tile) introduced a padding bug that manifests for long sequences when combined with aggressive KV delta caching. Will reproduce against v3.4-quant locally and on a dedicated dev-pool.

2026-03-11 - Evelyn Chen (SRE): Reproduced KV-cache desync on dedicated pool with workload replay. Dedicated worker logs show mismatch between cache key versions after a rolling runtime upgrade. Scoped reproducer and linked to PR: refs/pull/6421.

2026-03-11 - Marco Li: Implemented a hotfix patch (refs/pull/6421) to disable the auto-tile branch for quantized kernels; added fallback path to previous kernel selector. Deployed to canary in hosted-only as of 03:40 UTC.
2026-03-12 - On-call CS: Customer A (Dedicated tenant) escalated with truncated completions for chat sessions. Applied cache flush + worker restart as a temporary remediation while hotfix evaluated.

2026-03-12 - Marco Li: Observed improvements in hosted canary after hotfix: token truncation rate down 90% in canary window. However one Private customer reported OOMs when applying hotfix due to hw-software mismatch; paused automated rollout for Private.

2026-03-13 - Aisha Patel: Decided to pause all rollouts and mark v3.4-quant quarantined. Notifying sales/CS leadership and impacted customers with recommended rollback plan and ETA for further updates (timeline +21 hours).

2026-03-14 - Marco Li: Started orchestration checklist for multi-tenant rollback. Drafted control-plane changes to add 'canary-fail' trigger conditions (latency > baseline + 3 sigma OR token-drop-rate > 1%) and safe rollback window checks. Patch scheduled for review: refs/pull/6450.
2026-03-14 - Security (Ana Gomez): Confirmed no customer data exfiltration observed. Private patches must be signed; prepare release artifacts and HMAC checksums.

2026-03-14 - Marco Li: Next steps - complete PR review, coordinate Dedicated pool maintenance window with infra, prepare signed hotfix build for Private customers, and publish customer-facing status updates with CS by EOD 2026-03-14.
acceptance_criteria: All active rollouts of v3.4-quant are paused and quarantine flag set in model catalog.
Hosted canary clusters either have hotfix deployed or are rolled back to v3.3-stable; telemetry shows token-drop-rate <= baseline+0.5% for two consecutive 2-hour windows.
Dedicated tenant pools with reported regressions are isolated and remediated (cache flush + worker restart) and have a verified plan for full rollback if needed.
Private customers with regressions have a signed hotfix or rollback package delivered and a scheduled maintenance window; handoff documented with customer's infra lead.
Control-plane adds canary-fail triggers and automated rollback policy in a way that preserves safe-window checks and provides audit logs.
Customer communications sent and CS confirms reduced incoming escalations related to this regression.
resolution_summary: Ongoing. Patch rollout to hosted canary reduced token truncation by ~90%; full cross-env rollback paused and orchestrated. Private customers require signed artifact and manual coordination. Postmortem scheduled after stable rollout/rollback completion.
next_steps: 1) Merge control-plane rollback policy PR and deploy to staging. 2) Schedule Dedicated maintenance window with Infra and apply worker restart + cache flush. 3) Build and sign hotfix artifact for Private customers; coordinate delivery with Solutions and CS. 4) Run validation harness against long-context testset and confirm telemetry thresholds before un-quarantining any model variant.
